Stage 2: Manufacturing (Circuit boards & electronics)
Stage 3: Product Use (Device charging & operation)
Stage 4: Disposal (E-waste & recycling)

slides.title: LCA Core Terminology & Pathway
slides.text:
Life cycle analysis 
Life cycle analysis is a “cradle-to-grave” analysis of a product. There are four main stages of a product's life cycle: 
Raw materials 
- Extracting and processing the raw materials needed
Manufacturing
 - the product and its packaging
Use
 - Using the product during its lifetime
Disposal
 - Disposing of the product at the end of its useful life

slides.title: OCR Exam Checkpoint: 6-Mark Smartphone LCA (PDF Viewer)
slides.text:
Six mark Question 
A life cycle assessment assesses the environmental impact of products such as smartphones. Some activities in the life cycle of a smartphone are listed below. 
Extracting oil from oil wells
Making plastics from oil 
Obtaining copper from copper ore 
Putting together all the components 
Packing the phone in a box
Watching videos on the phone
Taking apart the phone
Recycling the copper from some of the phone components
Describe the four stages that are assessed in a life cycle assessment. 
In your answer, give at least one example from the list above for each stage. 
[6 marks]

slides.title: Model Answer & Mark Scheme Review
slides.text:
Six mark Question 
The four stages of life cycle analysis are extraction of raw material, 
manufacturing, 
use and disposal. 
Extracting oil from oil wells is an example of extraction, extraction of copper from copper ore is also another example of extraction. 
Making plastics from oil is an example of manufacturing. Packing the phone in a box is also an example of 
 manufacturing. 
Watching videos on the phone is an example of phone use. 
Taking apart the phone and then recycling the copper from some of the phone components is an example of how smartphones are disposed of.
